implemented_pending_full_acceptance: Close-owned year-end postings allowed while operational postings remain frozen; period row share lock coordinates posting with close.
Retainage discrepancies and absent or duplicate control evidence prevent close.
General invoices use on_invoice recognition; native income selections and cost codes flow to postings and proportional credit memos.
1099 paginates evidence, deduplicates payment links, filters reversals by settlement and occurrence date, and preserves card exclusions; missing legacy payment evidence blocks filing.
AR/AP aging and control checks share dated settlements, credit balances and stable pagination; AP respects bill cutoff and excludes withheld retainage.
Retainage controls reconstruct releases using dated source documents rather than current hold status or lifetime released amounts.

POC recognition posts only exact period-end snapshots, even for a close dated today; future recognition and backdated live snapshot capture are rejected. Service regression confirms stale/missing positions never post.

Close and recognition share dated financial-activity project scope, independent of current lifecycle status. Recognition compares the reviewed population and preflights all positions before any journal posts.
Close review pins immutable WIP snapshot identities, input hashes, amounts, dates and warnings; recognition verifies the same evidence and records its references on journal lines.

Accountants can inspect contract/cost/EAC/earned/billed/profit figures and approve specific WIP snapshots with an attributed explanation in the close workspace. Missing or changed review blocks close.

Atomic WIP review locks the accounting period, rejects stale/scoped/mismatched evidence, and permits only open/reopened periods. A snapshot insert guard freezes WIP evidence during review/closed periods.
Books export record now declares manifest schema version 3, and checksum streaming uses the storage API web stream contract.

Historical WIP preparation is available in the review dialog. Accountant-supplied period contract/change-order/EAC estimates are combined with a single database statement snapshot of dated costs, gross pretax billings, and credits.
Preparation preserves source rows, preparer, timestamp, basis explanation and prior snapshot linkage. Repeated unchanged preparation is idempotent; a reverted estimate creates a new revision.
Approval, close and recognition verify prepared source evidence against dated operational records. Late cost/billing/credit changes invalidate review until a new snapshot is prepared and approved.

Completed jobs can explicitly carry a fully earned, approved closed-period estimate forward after confirming no contract/estimate changes. The RPC compares dated source evidence, records prior snapshot/period links, and creates a current-period snapshot requiring new review; changed evidence blocks carryforward.

WIP earned revenue and completion ratios use exact integer rounding. Database preparation uses exact division, versions calculation inputs, and creates corrected revisions instead of returning older rounded snapshots. Invalid EAC/cost/budget inputs block review and recognition; snapshot evidence checks include calculated-value integrity.

Expected-loss provisions for one reviewed cost-to-cost construction contract post during close after reviewed revenue: full forecast loss less loss already incurred. The reserve releases as losses are incurred or estimates recover; retries reconcile to the ledger balance without duplicate postings.

Expected-loss journal lines preserve reviewed WIP snapshot/hash and target calculations. Distinct liability and COGS account subtypes are supported by the chart and database vocabulary; expected-loss expense is excluded from the actual-job-cost tie-out.

WIP approval and close preflight reject multiple primary contracts, conflicting system account codes, and expected-loss positions with capitalized costs needing impairment review. Posting repeats checks under period/project locks. These unsupported cases are explicit blockers, not completed workflows.

Books export schema 4 embeds verified binary supporting documents as base64 objects. Offline verification cross-checks file inventory, metadata, size, exact encoding and SHA-256; extraction restores documents into a fresh directory with path validation and no overwrites. Legacy schema 2/3 copied-file verification remains supported.

Exports now capture every allowlisted table through one read-only STABLE database RPC using a single statement MVCC snapshot. Organization filtering, deterministic row order and full row aggregation are applied within the database; capture timestamp and visibility identifier accompany the archive. Browser roles cannot invoke capture; service authorization remains required.

Bank statement creation and date/balance edits now enforce organization/account scope, contiguous continuation of the last closed statement, matching opening balance, nonoverlap and safe integer cents under a bank-account lock. New statements cannot be created while another is open, and closed dates/balances require reopening before changes.

Bank close evidence version 2 preserves statement transaction IDs, dates, descriptions, amounts, exclusions and confirmed match amounts in its hashed proof. Closed detail uses these saved rows without querying current feeds. Older evidence retains totals/outstanding lines with an explicit unavailable-description notice; missing closed evidence blocks historical display.
Projection failures recognize both original and newer database closed-period error wording, preserving actionable closed-period findings instead of generic retry failures.

Export recovery verification uses exact integer journal totals, rejects unsafe/fractional/negative/dual-sided/zero-sided line amounts, requires row identities even when checksums agree, and requires a versioned manifest for offline archive verification. Canonical bigint strings are validated within PostgreSQL bigint range.

Regular projection job now persists source-specific reconciliation failures with cures instead of waiting for nightly maintenance. Incremental passes enumerate evaluated source keys and resolve only findings for those sources. Global resolution requires both an explicit full-run request and completed full scan, so disabled/skipped work cannot erase findings. Organization enumeration is paginated deterministically.

Projection receipts record the observed source timestamp and validated posted fact/journal on successful or unchanged projection. The server-only RPC scopes evidence by organization/source and prevents stale observations overwriting newer receipts. Export schema 5 includes receipts and preserves verification/extraction support for schemas 2–4.

Shared Arc ledger status is embedded in invoice accounting details and the payable workspace. Scoped service authorization precedes ledger reads, with organization-wide Books access for sources without a project. Status combines unresolved failures, current journal state and exact microsecond source/receipt timestamps; users can refresh. Missing or stale evidence never claims posted.

Invoice line insert/update/delete/reassignment now invalidates invoice source timestamps. Invoice, bill and expense headers use a final monotonic microsecond update trigger after legacy timestamp triggers, preventing revision regressions under old transaction timestamps. Existing bill/expense child triggers inherit this guarantee.
The shared posting-status component now also appears in expense detail, using expense project bill-read authorization and the same receipt/failure state model as invoice and payable workflows.

Revenue basis no longer depends on contract row order: draft/superseded contracts, child amendments and contracts effective after the cutoff are excluded. All eligible primary contracts must agree on recognition basis; conflicts block Books with the project identity. Historical WIP population passes its accounting cutoff to this shared resolution. When only superseded primary evidence remains at a cutoff, resolution blocks instead of silently falling back to POC.

Reviewed WIP supports native income-account allocations with contract and cost-code dimensions. A scoped service-only atomic RPC creates immutable allocation revisions, validates active income accounts and full contract-value coverage, preserves preparer/explanation, and invalidates earlier approval. The review workspace displays and edits these allocations.

POC posting uses exact cumulative allocation targets minus prior account/dimension balances, including zero-net reclassifications and estimate reductions. Recognition and expected-loss verification share income lineage across native recognition journals and their reversals, preserve legacy 4000 balances, and exclude year-end closing and unrelated custom income.

Estimate revisions retain allocations when contract value is unchanged. Changed contract value requires a new allocation before WIP approval/recognition; this requirement persists through further revisions. Completed-job carryforward preserves approved allocations. Current account-code/type/activation and dimension scope changes invalidate the WIP gate.

New direct payment/deposit and reversal facts capture versioned payment-to-invoice/bill ownership. The evidence participates in economic hashes and deterministic replay adds payment/document dimensions to every journal line. Invalid or mismatched source-document evidence blocks the specific candidate. Unchanged legacy facts are preserved without fabricated historical ownership; actual economic/date revisions capture current evidence.

Version 2 settlement evidence captures full multi-document payment allocations, scopes each target to the organization, takes project ownership from the document, and requires exact payment coverage and one AR/AP side. The projector can classify an allocation-only payment; invalid/partial, cross-project or deposit allocations produce blockers rather than invented ownership.

Allocated payment replay splits AR/AP, fee/discount/recovery and cash lines by immutable document/project allocations. Cash is the residual of each allocation, so both journal totals and each project remain balanced through cent rounding. Every line carries payment/allocation/document dimensions and captured project relationships.

Payment headers now use a final monotonic revision trigger. Allocation insert/update/delete and reassignment touch both scoped parent payments, bringing child changes into incremental projection. A blocked live allocation or classification retains every prior owned payment posting type during full-scan retirement; it does not erase real cash because evidence became invalid.

Cash-method invoice settlement allocator separates income from collected sales-tax liabilities using immutable document basis IDs and complete dated applied principal. Cumulative cutoff allocation preserves monthly/annual cents, signed native income/discount buckets and exact refunds. Grouped tax allocation avoids a backward tax-cent rounding hazard. Incomplete/mismatched/duplicate evidence, advance receipts, unapplied amounts and unsafe cents block computation. This engine is not yet wired to a complete cash-method P&L.

Invoice header revision, lines and native income selections now come from a service-only STABLE invoker RPC in one MVCC snapshot. Capture exhausts all lines and compares exact microsecond source revision before projecting. New invoice facts retain POC income components without changing deferred accrual posting; unchanged legacy facts remain unchanged and require reviewed historical attribution. Frozen facts supply cash income/tax basis with retained principal and project/cost-code dimensions. Fully retained progress invoices no longer disappear because their net amount is zero.

Cash invoice settlement extraction follows posted/reversed AR journal principal and frozen direct/allocated document ownership. It includes original and reversing entries to cancel corrections before replacements, preserves actual refund payment ownership, excludes draft journals, checks original fact/source IDs and rejects absent evidence, amount drift, duplicate original journals and invalid reversal lineage. Frozen-document cash calculation integration is covered; complete organization history/source reconciliation and report loading remain.

Cash invoice income supporting service now authorizes organization-wide Books read before capturing one STABLE export snapshot. Pure snapshot assembly reconciles settled payments/refunds against posted AR principal, requires current invoice/payment/refund receipts with exact journal/fact/source association, ties frozen invoice gross/tax/native or deferred income to its original journal, preserves provenance and computes cumulative cash income. Missing sources, stale receipts, foreign rows, legacy evidence, credits/writeoffs, advance policies, revised tax/income and retainage aliases block rather than produce partial totals. This remains an invoice-income supporting service, not the full cash-method P&L.

Full-schema cash invoice income drill executes actual atomic invoice/payment/refund projection, projection receipts and export snapshot RPCs. General and POC invoices share an allocated receipt while preserving native accounts/job dimensions; processor fees remain separate, real reversal/repost fee corrections do not double count income, and later refunds preserve prior-month cutoff. Real schema exposed and corrected the refund-status mismatch: reconciliation now uses succeeded, not posted. All fixtures roll back and org/user absence is explicitly verified.

Journal lines now capture authoritative posted account code/type/subtype/normal-balance/cash-flow classification in immutable dimensions. Reversals inherit original classification and dimensions even after chart recoding; missing legacy classification is explicitly unknown. Exact reversal guards require every original line with identical account/job/counterparty and opposite amounts, preventing balanced wrong-account or subset reversals. Counts are checked at posting/commit and support both immediate and deferred constraint callers. Existing posted-line immutability errors are preserved.

Paid-bill support now derives native job costs, overhead expenses and capitalized purchases from original posted account classifications and construction dimensions. Cumulative cutoff allocations conserve exact cents through installments, corrections and supplier refunds. Gross AP relief is retained separately from payment discounts, avoiding double discount deductions. Vendor settlement extraction supports frozen direct and multi-bill allocations. Unknown legacy classifications, supplier advances, accrued use-tax attribution, invalid/ambiguous journal evidence and excess principal block. This supporting calculation is not yet the complete reconciled paid-cost service or cash P&L.

Cash invoice snapshot assembly now uses captured original account codes when available, so live chart recoding cannot rewrite posted cash-income classification. Explicit legacy-unknown snapshots never fall back to current chart codes. Reviewed pre-migration classification mapping and historic accrual statement consumption remain.

Paid-bill costs now have an authorized server service using the same single MVCC export snapshot for operational bills/payments/allocations/refunds, immutable facts, posted journals and projection receipts. It reconciles principal separately for each payment and each bill, validates actual succeeded supplier refunds and complete allocation coverage, bounds refunds to original payment/bill principal, rejects missing/stale/orphan/duplicate evidence, and ties native cost basis to one original bill journal. Revised cost classifications require historical attribution rather than rewriting earlier paid costs. Credit applications, noncash/card funding, accrued use tax and retainage aliases require explicit reviewed policies/linkage. Per-source indexes avoid scanning all journals for each bill/payment. Supporting service still needs report UI and full cash P&L policy integration.
Cash invoice income now recognizes the operational paid payment status consistently with the projector; its regression verifies paid receipts produce income rather than a false completeness failure.

Direct cash-paid expenses now derive signed COGS, overhead and capitalized purchases from actual frozen journal classifications, including original/correcting/replacement lineage. The single-snapshot calculator validates source totals, exact current receipts, journal/fact dates and IDs, organization ownership, duplicate originals/reversals and native account totals. Card/reimbursement liability funding and missing legacy classification require review. Prior postings that ignored saved native account coding block instead of being silently relabeled. A combined authorized accounting-activity service loads one MVCC snapshot and passes that same revision to invoice income, bill costs and direct-expense calculations. This is supporting activity, not a complete cash P&L.

Standalone expense fact replay now preserves explicit native account selections and captured dimensions; uncoded overhead portions retain the existing Other expense default. Earlier immutable incorrectly classified journals are not automatically rewritten. The full operational nonproject expense workflow and reviewed repair path still need acceptance.

Vendor-bill and expense cost-line totals, and the shared journal balance validator, now sum integer cents with BigInt. Journal validation detects an actual one-cent imbalance previously masked by floating-point aggregate rounding and rejects balanced totals that cannot be represented safely in the existing numeric total contract.

Export schema 6 adds previously omitted payment-run fee-charge sources to the same service-only STABLE MVCC snapshot. The export manifest/checksum/relationship verifier now includes fee run and funding-source links, requires fee history for version 6, and preserves version 2-5 archive compatibility. Embedded document verification and extraction accept version 6. Unknown schema versions now explicitly fail rather than bypassing table validation. Actual full-schema Arc Pay fee source and atomic posting are captured and the generated snapshot passes schema 6 recovery integrity; full cash P&L consumption and broader recovery acceptance remain.

Cash accounting activity now includes a separate settlement-ancillary calculation on the same captured MVCC snapshot. It derives processor/AP fee expenses, customer fee recoveries and supplier discounts from frozen original/reversing/replacement journals, validates exact fact amounts and balanced journal cents, preserves project/company dimensions, and reconciles live receipt split-versus-rollup fees and gross recoveries. Separate Arc Pay charges require scoped run/funding ownership, actual settled dates and current receipts; omitted, stale, orphaned, duplicate, unbalanced, legacy/unclassified and unsupported funding evidence block. Gross invoice/bill principal is unchanged and ancillary amounts are counted once. Historical source revisions, complete operational discount capture and full cash P&L policies remain.

Actual schema-based recovery preflight now enumerates required missing values, generated/unknown columns, complete composite foreign keys including MATCH FULL partial-null failures, and exact organization/user/external dependencies. It verifies archive integrity before inspection and labels only readiness for a restore attempt, not restoration success. An offline CLI reads gzip/plain archives and catalog JSON, emits a new private mapping report without overwrites, and never writes to a database. Full-schema catalog evidence and a real rolled-back insert prove that the export service’s redacted funding rows cannot be restored without provider_customer_id and other required values. Explicit identity dependencies and disconnected funding restoration now pass the populated isolated restore described below; self-contained identity export and broader recovery coverage remain required.

Offline restore-plan preparation now accepts explicit organization/app-user/disabled-auth dependencies, validates their target schema and foreign keys, rejects live credentials/tokens, and requires reviewed funding actor mappings. It preserves the original checksummed archive, omits generated columns for target recomputation, disables/disconnects restored provider funding, and records deterministic plan/source digests plus each field change. The CLI writes a new private plan without overwriting evidence. A current full-schema isolated drill restores populated invoice/payment/refund/vendor-bill/direct-expense/fee sources and immutable journals, checks every actual FK for populated groups, compares archived tables including regenerated values, and reproduces four cash activity calculations. A source document extracts with exact bytes and restored invoice linkage. Normal triggers are re-enabled; a new project expense posts atomically and has the expected receipt and cash cost. Both original and restoration transactions roll back with fixture absence verified. Other populated modules, object storage, production orchestration and browser acceptance remain.

Native cash P&L is now exposed as books-cash-profit-loss in the Financial statements report catalog alongside separate accrual P&L and Operating Cash reconciliation. One authorized service-only MVCC snapshot composes native invoice collections/refunds, paid supplier costs/refunds, direct expense corrections and fees/recoveries/discounts. BigInt totals preserve original account classifications and construction dimensions; sales tax and capitalized purchases stay outside P&L. Source detail links to actual billing/payables/expense URLs, with original fact/document evidence carried in CSV. Every posted historical journal through cutoff requires frozen account classification and complete balanced lines. Unhandled cash/P&L history blocks publication; noncash POC/year-end exclusions require native journal kinds. Net income plus collected tax less capitalized purchases must equal actual posted cash movement. Actual full-schema drill verifies -250 cents net income +455 tax -400 capitalization = -195 cash, monthly telescoping, restored P&L equality and a new expense reducing net income by exactly 111 cents. Nine focused calculation/service/catalog/CSV regressions pass. This does not complete broader cash policies or tax adjustments, browser/PDF/run transport, payroll/entities or full builder acceptance.

Tax adjustments now have a separate immutable cash workpaper backend. Preparation freezes canonical economic evidence and a cutoff-specific database source revision; unrelated future transactions preserve prior basis, while changed posted/current eligible cash sources block preparation/review. Signed permanent/timing lines require exact safe cents, scope, rationale and evidence reference. An active preparer and different active reviewer, substantive non-null notes, exact-period approval uniqueness, idempotent retries and atomic replacement preserve original reviewed history. Actual service-role invoker path passes SQL tests. Authorized services/actions and a distinct tax adjustment report bridge are registered with workpaper/basis/preparer/reviewer trace fields. No operational facts or accrual journals are posted. Schema 7 recovery captures workpapers and validates basis digests, nested file/project references and separate review; schema 2-6 compatibility and embedded document recovery pass. Preparation/review UI, populated native tax/report/restore acceptance, immutable attachment version/checksum capture and complete report transport remain incomplete.

Tax page now includes exact-period workpaper loading, signed permanent/timing adjustment preparation with evidence references, immutable draft retries, independent-review controls, replacement preparation retaining original approval until review, stale-basis warnings and correctly dated reviewed report links. Authorized workspace service captures one source context, verifies stored basis integrity and returns only display evidence, not the full historical basis. Browser-safe schemas/calculation are separated from server hashing. Service tests exercise denied reads, current/stale workspace state, tamper rejection and reviewed report publication; browser transport and attachment identity remain unverified.

Tax workpapers now support explicit independently reviewed no-adjustment confirmations with substantive immutable preparation evidence and no artificial zero-value adjustment. Service-only audited withdrawal closes draft workpapers with actor/date/reason, preserves history and original replacement-target approval, supports exact retry and rejects withdrawal of approved records. Tax UI and report expose preparation/closure explanations; schema 7 export verification requires rationale for empty adjustment arrays and preserves older nonempty workpaper compatibility. Full-schema 16-assertion SQL controls include actual service role review/withdrawal; browser and populated native tax workpaper recovery remain pending.

Populated native tax acceptance and schema 7 recovery now pass against the isolated full-schema PostgreSQL database: posted construction cash sources produce a canonical basis, actual service-role preparation/review records signed adjustments, a no-adjustments replacement supersedes the original, a duplicate replacement is withdrawn, and a new dated expense blocks stale review/publication. All three archived workpaper versions restore exactly with explicit actor dependencies, FK checks, disabled funding and original supporting document bytes. Actual tax service/report/CSV execute on captured native evidence through an adapted context/transport. Browser/HTTP/report-run/PDF and review-time attachment byte identity remain unfinished. Docker commands in the native runner now have bounded execution time.

Tax attachment metadata is now frozen in immutable adjustment lines and original bytes are streamed/verified before preparation, review and publication. Attached legacy workpapers without frozen proof require replacement. Optional document selector and CSV version/checksum/path evidence are implemented. New SQL guards lock capture metadata and protect referenced version/document history, but final database tests/replay are pending Docker recovery. Schema 7 now explicitly refuses old attachment recovery when its original bytes are absent; historical-object export support still needs implementation.

Posted payroll claims minimal source ownership and protects consumed original time wage/cost inputs, native job costs, posting receipts and original labor journals from independent economic changes or reversal. Existing source RLS permits operational ownership access without salary/register access. Notes, approved statuses, invoice links and projection refreshes remain available.

Export schema 13 proves exact original native payroll ownership and rejects forged, duplicate, orphan or drifted sources. Older schema 12 posted archives may derive explicit checksummed recovery mappings only from intact reviewed native evidence. Generated insertion values retain verified archive evidence for accounting preflight and post-insert comparison.

Source-verified replacement payroll correction preview compares actual posted provider registers, creates balanced signed GL/project/overhead deltas without consuming native wages again, preserves customer billing/cash, and exposes per-worker overpayment, additional attribution and changed budget/billing/tax review dependencies. Immutable correction versions/review/posting remain unfinished.

Corrected provider source preparation, independent review, withdrawal and documentary revision history are private and immutable; actual SQL independently validates controls/scopes/retained documents/accounts, and source review does not post money. Schema 14 includes source histories and retained CSV replay/restoration. Correction monetary proposals/commit and full shared acceptance remain unfinished.
